To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EOF of a yield stress fluid can be enhanced in the channel patterned with uncharged free slipping patches and no slip charged patches.

the EOF enhancement is achieved in the modulated nanochannels by the periodic arrangement of the slip and no slip patches, and that the enhancement is higher for the Herschel Bulkly fluid compared with the Newtonian fluid.

the electroosmotive flow of a viscopastic yield-stress fluid can be enhanced by the presence of uncharged slipping surfaces embedded on the walls of a microfluidic channel, and the enhancement is higher for a shear thinning fluid than for a power law fluid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electroosmotive flow of a Herschel-Bulkley fluid within a nanochannel patterned with periodically placed slipping and charged surfaces.
the study of electroosmotic (EOF) flow of a Herschel Bulkely fluid within a slit channel patterned with a periodic arrangement of slipping surfaces and no-slip charged surfaces embedded on its walls.
the study of a viscoplatic fluid within a slit channel modulated by periodically placed slipping surfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present work has shown that the electroosmotive flow of visco plastic fluid in a nanoscale channel patterned with periodic uncharged slipping surfaces is significantly enhanced compared to the unmodified channel.
the channel can serve as an enhanced EOF and current density device for the non Newtonian yield-stress fluid.

the present study demonstrates the feasibility of achieving enhanced EOF of yield stress fluid by modulating the channel walls with periodic uncharged slipping surfaces, which can be potentially useful in the design of nanofluidic devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a numerical model for EOF of a Herschel Bulkely fluid within a nanochannel patterned with periodically distributed uncharged free slip and no slip charged surface.
the EOF enhancement in the modulate channel is higher for yield stress fluid compared to power law fluid and the boundary slip has significant impact on shear thinning fluid.
we can achieve a high electroosmotic flux of a viscoplastc fluid by patterning the channel wall with uncharged slip stripes and charged no slip stripes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a significant EOF enhancement and cation selectivity can be achieved in a modulated nanochannel with a non Newtonian electrolytes, which is a promising approach for lab on a chip applications.
the channel can serve as a cation selective device when the slip length and planform length are comparable with the channel height.
a modulated channel patterned with uncharged slipping surfaces can be used to enhance the EOF of a non-Newtonian electrolyte.
